metadata.scenario_context: Various global tech firms are partnering on a project and have chosen to convene a joint forum to evaluate their work progress in mid-April. To express her disagreement with the newly-toppled president, John has decided to participate in a strike.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from Canada strongly disagree they would never join strikes.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Libya strongly agree they would never join strikes.

agent_1.goal_1: Discuss the potential scheduling of the joint forum on April 19th.
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether it is common to discuss or join strikes as a form of protest.

agent_2.goal_1: Talk about a specific date for the forum.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether it is common to join strikes as a form of protest.

shared_prefix.speaker: Maria
shared_prefix.message:
Hey Sara, have you heard anything about the joint forum scheduled for April 19th? I think we need to finalize the details soon.

Also, I'm curious about something... Is it really common to discuss or join strikes as a form of protest? I just can't wrap my head around that approach.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Sara
shared_prefix.message:
Yes, I heard about the forum on April 19th. It's important we finalize everything before then. 

As for strikes... well, from my perspective, people in Libya wouldn't typically consider joining strikes. It's just not something that's commonly done. There are other ways to express disagreement that are more aligned with our values.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Maria
shared_prefix.message:
I agree that we need to finalize everything before the forum. It's crucial for our project.

But, about strikes... I'm still surprised that people would choose that route to express their views. In Canada, we strongly disagree with joining strikes. I wonder what drives people to take that step.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Sara
shared_prefix.message: Actually, in our way, strikes aren't a proper method of protest. They create division and chaos, not understanding. People in Libya focus on unity and expressing disagreement through dialogue—not disruption. It's just not in our culture to take that route. I find it surprising that others think strikes are effective. No, that's not how it works. It's more constructive to work together, not against each other.
shared_prefix.label: Defense

turns.speaker: Maria
